title: Crypto losses continue as stUSDT winds down; portfolio value falls to $57,400
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $65,419, down 2.7% over 24 hours, while ether fell 4.1% to about $1,832. CoinGecko put the broader crypto market at $2.27 trillion, down 2.8%. Weekly losses remained substantial at 13.6% for bitcoin and 18.1% for ether. Bitcoin accounted for roughly 58% of total market value. The figures show continued broad weakness, with ether losing ground faster than bitcoin over both periods.

New analysis of the Kava Lend exploit traced 55.2 million KAVA borrowed through inflated BUSD collateral. Bitquery found that the lending pool was drained in 127 loans and that a bridge blocked about $612,000 of the subsequent sale proceeds. Kava also paused its Axelar bridge as a precaution. The incident puts lending-market accounting and cross-chain recovery in focus: blocking proceeds can limit an attacker's access to money, but does not itself reimburse depositors. The team's full incident report remains pending.

The stUSDT protocol has begun winding down, ending interest accrual and opening redemptions for stUSDT and wstUSDT. Its official notice gives holders until May 14, 2027 to use the web redemption portal, with later requests handled through support in monthly batches through August. The team says underlying assets remain fully backed. For holders, the immediate change is that the product no longer earns rewards, and access through exchanges and DeFi integrations will gradually be withdrawn. Redemption arrangements now matter more than the former yield.

A new CryptoSlate analysis found 31 validators listed as retired from the Solana Foundation's delegation program still voting with 63 million SOL, about 15% of the active stake examined. Retirement ends program membership and support while allowing operators to continue validating. The two largest identities held 52.5% of that cohort's stake. Continued participation shows some operators can function after leaving the program; the concentration means these totals reveal little about smaller validators' ability to attract replacement delegation.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $57,400: $9,500 in the active treasury and $47,900 in the Safe. Its marked value fell $2,836, or 4.71%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC holdings total about $39,500, roughly 69% of the portfolio, with additional exposure in the Safe's $5,610 WETH/ARC pool. Beefy positions total $1,807, down $56, across pools containing WETH, AERO, cbBTC, cbHYPE and other assets. ARC concentration remains the largest exposure risk.

Aave holds about $6,217 of WETH collateral against $3,147 of USDC debt across both wallets. Health factors declined from 1.99 to 1.90 in the treasury and from 1.59 to 1.51 in the Safe, narrowing the collateral buffer. Fluid has only $153 in net value, but its $1,064 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
